message.content:
Confirmed! In `constructXRef`, when an entry is created (line ~930), it sets `offset`, `gen`, and `type`, but does NOT set `flags`. The `flags` field remains uninitialized. Then when `Parser::makeStream` calls `entry->setFlag(XRefEntry::Parsing, true)`, it reads `flags` (via `flags |= mask`), which is uninitialized memory.

Now let me look at the existing PoC or seed corpus to understand the PDF format:
